description: How computer science research is planned, done, evaluated and communicated, from a question to a defended proposal and a final-year project that can withstand review. Taught to the depth of a graduate research methods seminar, with every stage practised on the student's own project.
modelledOn: Dawson, Projects in Computing and Information Systems: A Student's Guide
Creswell and Creswell, Research Design: Qualitative, Quantitative and Mixed Methods Approaches
ACM Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
outcomes: Distinguish scientific knowledge from opinion and classify research by purpose, method and contribution.
Find, read, critique and synthesise the literature on a topic and write a structured literature review.
Formulate research questions and hypotheses and choose an appropriate research design.
Plan a project with scope, milestones, risks and ethical approval.
Collect and analyse quantitative and qualitative data with the correct statistics and reporting.
Write a research proposal and project report and present and defend the work.

units.title: Overview of research and scientific knowledge
topics: What research is: systematic inquiry, reproducibility, falsifiability; science versus engineering versus design
Kinds of knowledge and sources of truth; the scientific method and its limits
Research in computer science: theory, experiments, systems building, empirical software engineering, human studies
Contributions: new algorithms, tools, evidence, taxonomies; what counts as novelty
Reading a research paper: structure, claims, evidence, limitations

units.title: Research as communication
topics: Venues: journals, conferences, workshops, preprints; peer review and impact
Scientific writing: clarity, precision, structure, citing; avoiding plagiarism
Reference management (Zotero, BibTeX) and citation styles (ACM, IEEE, APA)
Presenting: talks, posters, demonstrations; writing for non-experts and funders

units.title: Ethics
topics: Research integrity: fabrication, falsification, plagiarism, authorship, conflicts of interest
Human participants: informed consent, anonymity, data protection (Ghana's Data Protection Act), vulnerable groups
Ethics review boards and institutional approval; ethics in AI, security and data research
Responsible use of generative AI in research and writing

units.title: Types of research projects
topics: Basic and applied; exploratory, descriptive, explanatory, evaluative
Quantitative, qualitative and mixed methods; experiments, surveys, case studies, action research, design science
Development projects versus research projects; the artefact plus evaluation model
Choosing a topic: feasibility, interest, supervisor fit, local relevance

units.title: Literature review and critique
topics: Searching: databases (ACM DL, IEEE Xplore, Google Scholar, arXiv), keywords, snowballing, inclusion criteria
Systematic literature reviews and mapping studies; keeping a search log
Critical appraisal: validity, sample, methods, bias, reproducibility
Synthesis: themes, gaps, tables of comparison; writing the review, not a list of summaries
Workshop: reviewing ten papers on the student's topic

units.title: Research and project planning
topics: From topic to research questions, aims, objectives and hypotheses; scope and boundaries
Work plans, Gantt charts, milestones, deliverables, supervision meetings
Risk assessment and contingency; resources, tools and data access
Time management and keeping a research diary

units.title: Research design and data collection
topics: Variables, operationalisation, validity (internal, external, construct) and reliability
Experimental design: controls, randomisation, between and within subjects, benchmarks for algorithm and system evaluation
Surveys and questionnaires; interviews and focus groups; observation; sampling strategies
Measurement in computing: performance metrics, usability metrics (SUS), accuracy metrics
Pilot studies and pre-registration

units.title: Data analysis
topics: Descriptive statistics and visualisation; choosing the right chart
Inferential statistics: t-tests, ANOVA, chi-square, correlation, regression, non-parametric tests; effect sizes and confidence intervals; p-value pitfalls
Qualitative analysis: coding, thematic analysis, grounded theory in brief
Tools: R, Python, SPSS, NVivo; reproducible analysis scripts
Threats to validity and how to report them honestly

units.title: Structure of a research proposal
topics: Title, abstract, introduction and motivation, problem statement, research questions, objectives
Literature review, methodology, expected outcomes, timeline, budget, references
Writing and peer-reviewing proposals in class; responding to feedback
Proposal defence

units.title: Structure of a research project report
topics: Chapters: introduction, literature review, methodology, design and implementation, results and evaluation, discussion, conclusion and future work
Appendices, code and data availability, reproducibility packages
Figures, tables and captions; abstracts and executive summaries
Final presentation and viva preparation; turning a project into a paper
